title: Lecture 1: Introduction to Python for Data Science
notes: Why Python for Data Science: package ecosystem (NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn).
Jupyter notebooks and interactive computing environment.
Data types, arithmetic expressions, and variable assignment.

transcript.text: Welcome to Python for Data Science. I am Prof. Raghunathan Rengasamy from IIT Madras.
Data science combines statistical domain expertise with algorithmic computation.
We set up Python and Jupyter environments for rapid exploratory analysis.

title: Lecture 2: Core Python Syntax, Sequences & Control
concept_name: Lists, Tuples & Loops in Data Processing
notes: Lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets for structured data storage.
List comprehensions for concise, vectorized-style element processing.
Conditional branching and iterative loops for batch processing.

transcript.text: Today we cover data structures: lists, dictionaries, and list comprehensions.
List comprehensions offer a fast and expressive syntax for transforming data records.
Iterating over collections and applying filter criteria.

title: Lecture 3: Introduction to NumPy & Multidimensional Arrays
notes: The NumPy ndarray: homogeneous contiguous memory layout for high performance.
Creating arrays: arange, linspace, zeros, ones, and eye.
Broadcasting rules in multidimensional arithmetic operations.

transcript.text: Week 2 introduces NumPy, the core library for scientific computing in Python.
Python lists store pointer references, while NumPy ndarrays store raw typed bytes in contiguous memory.
Broadcasting allows arithmetic between arrays of different but compatible shapes without copying data.

title: Lecture 4: NumPy Array Indexing, Slicing & Operations
notes: Multi-axis indexing and strides.
Boolean masking and fancy indexing for conditional subsetting.
Matrix operations: dot product, matrix inversion, and singular value decomposition.

transcript.text: In this lecture we demonstrate advanced slicing, boolean masks, and matrix algebra with NumPy.
Boolean masks filter rows matching criteria in a single vectorized step.
np.dot and np.linalg functions execute optimized BLAS/LAPACK routines.

module_title: Week 3: Tabular Data Processing with Pandas
title: Lecture 5: Pandas DataFrames & Data Cleaning
notes: Series and DataFrame data structures.
Reading CSV, Excel, and SQL data sources.
Handling missing data: isnull, dropna, fillna with statistical imputation.

transcript.text: Pandas is the primary library for data manipulation and tabular analysis in Python.
A DataFrame represents a 2D table with labeled axes: row index and column names.
Cleaning messy data: identifying nulls and imputing sensible defaults.

module_title: Week 3: Tabular Data Processing with Pandas
title: Lecture 6: Exploratory Data Analysis & Aggregations
notes: The Split-Apply-Combine strategy with groupby.
Aggregation functions: mean, median, standard deviation, and custom aggregators.
Pivot tables and multi-index hierarchical data manipulation.

transcript.text: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) reveals patterns and anomalies before model training.
The groupby paradigm splits rows by category, computes summary metrics, and concatenates results.
Building pivot tables to cross-tabulate multi-attribute survey datasets.

title: Lecture 7: Data Visualization with Matplotlib & Seaborn
notes: Matplotlib figure and axes object hierarchy.
Line charts, scatter plots, histograms, and box plots for distribution diagnostics.
Statistical plotting with Seaborn: heatmaps, pairplots, and regression curves.

transcript.text: Visualizing distributions is essential for diagnosing skewness, outliers, and collinearity.
We construct histograms and boxplots to examine quantiles and extreme values.
Seaborn correlation heatmaps identify redundant collinear features.

title: Lecture 8: Applied Data Science Pipeline & Case Study
notes: End-to-end data science project lifecycle: ingest, clean, explore, model, interpret.
Feature engineering and scaling (MinMax vs StandardScaler).
Baseline regression and classification evaluation with metrics.

transcript.text: In our final lecture, we assemble the complete data pipeline on a real industrial dataset.
From raw messy CSV records to engineered features, visual diagnostics, and baseline models.
Summary of course principles and roadmap toward advanced predictive modeling.
